title: Composition isomorphism of derived pullbacks of module objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and $f\colon X\to Y$, $g\colon Y\to Z$ morphisms of schemes. There is a natural isomorphism
$$
L(g\circ f)^*\cong Lf^*\circ Lg^*\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Z})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})
$$
of derived pullbacks ([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]), induced by the underived composition isomorphism $(g\circ f)^*\cong f^*\circ g^*$ of [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp].

proof.text: Put $h=g\circ f$, $\mathcal A_T=\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$, $F_a=a^*$ and $L_a=La^*$ for $a=f,g,h$, using [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. By [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main] each $F_a$ is additive and exact. Write $Q_T:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A_T)\to D(\mathcal A_T)$ for the quasi-isomorphism localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and $C(F_a)$ for termwise application. The total left derived pair has counit $\epsilon_a:L_aQ_S\to Q_TC(F_a)$ and is a right Kan extension along $Q_S$ ([lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]).

source.place: First sentence: exactness of the full module-object pullbacks

proof.text: For $a:T\to S$, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] supplies $D_a$ and $\varphi_a:D_aQ_S\cong Q_TC(F_a)$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] makes this a right Kan pair. Apply [lem-sfb-right-kan-extension-unique-iso] to it and $(L_a,\epsilon_a)$: there is a canonical $u_a:L_a\cong D_a$ with $\varphi_a(u_aQ_S)=\epsilon_a$. Thus $p_a:=\epsilon_a$ is an isomorphism, being a composite of isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), left-derived exact-functor principle; canonical comparison by Mathlib rightKanExtensionUnique

proof.text: Let $b:F_h\cong F_fF_g$ be [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. Its components give a chain isomorphism $B_K:C(F_h)K\cong C(F_f)C(F_g)K$: the chain-map equation $F_fF_g(d^n)b_{K^n}=b_{K^{n+1}}F_h(d^n)$ is naturality of $b$. Its inverse is degreewise $b^{-1}$, and naturality at the components of a chain map makes $B$ natural in $K$.

source.place: Second sentence: the specified underived isomorphism on cochain complexes

proof.text: Set $q_K=p_{f,C(F_g)K}\circ L_f(p_{g,K})$ and $t_K=q_K^{-1}\circ Q_X(B_K)\circ p_{h,K}$. These are natural isomorphisms, with $t:L_hQ_Z\cong L_fL_gQ_Z$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], with identity factorization isomorphisms, descends $t$ uniquely to an isomorphism $c:L_h\cong L_fL_g$; the two composites invert quasi-isomorphisms because $Q_Z$ does. Its component equation $q_K\circ c_{Q_ZK}=Q_X(B_K)\circ p_{h,K}$ specifies precisely the comparison induced by $b$.
